privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.kidsListen: Listen to the privacy notice for children
privacy.kidsText: ReadBuddy remembers your name, your student number and how your reading practice goes, so it can give you the right exercises. Only your teacher can see your results. Other children cannot see them. We never show ads.
privacy.who.p: ReadBuddy is a reading practice service used by schools. The school, through the teacher, decides to use ReadBuddy for its students; the operator of the service processes the data described here on the school's behalf.
privacy.what.p: For teachers: name, e-mail address and password (stored only as a salted hash). For students, entered by the teacher: name, student number, birth year and practice language; plus reading settings, current levels, exercise results, stars, failed-login count, paused exercises (up to 24 hours) and assignments. Pictures uploaded by teachers must not show people; they are stored with an image-hosting service.
privacy.why.p: To give students reading practice at the right level and to show their progress to their teacher. ReadBuddy does not diagnose reading difficulties.
privacy.where.p: All personal data is stored and processed within the European Economic Area and encrypted at rest. Text to be read aloud is processed by a speech service without any information about who the student is — no names or student numbers.
privacy.how_long.p: Until the teacher removes the student or deletes their teacher account. Deleted data is removed from the service immediately and from backups within 30 days. If a student has not logged in for 24 months, their data is deleted; the teacher is e-mailed 30 days before.
privacy.rights.p: Students and their families can contact the school. The teacher can view, correct, download (JSON) and delete the stored data of their students at any time. You can also complain to the data protection authority.
privacy.not.p: No advertising, no in-app purchases, no tracking or analytics cookies, no chat between children, and no comparison of children with each other.

e4.intro: A picture exercise is one sentence with three pictures: the matching picture and two that do not match. Students get it when their E4 level and language match, or when you assign it. Items of the same level and language are played together.
e4.rule: Pictures must not show identifiable people — this includes students.
